LESSON: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading, part of Strand 4 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we read silently? 2. What makes a book interesting to read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. infer the meaning of vocabulary from context for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension,

   Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. infer the meaning of vocabulary from context for comprehension,

   Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure.

   Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. create a collection of simple Indigenous Languages readers for the class library,

2. conduct a readers’ theatre to read the class indigenous books in the collection,

3. work jointly to build a list of proverbs and sayings from the readers,

4. tease out vocabulary from the readers,

5. use simple level dictionaries to look up the meaning of vocabulary,

6. work jointly to fill code word tables or crossword puzzles using vocabulary,

7. team up to establish a reading club for the class to collect and read varied readers. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. create a collection of simple Indigenous Languages readers for the class library,
2. conduct a readers’ theatre to read the class indigenous books in the collection,
3. work jointly to build a list of proverbs and sayings from the readers,
4. tease out vocabulary from the readers,
5. use simple level dictionaries to look up the meaning of vocabulary,
6. work jointly to fill code word tables or crossword puzzles using vocabulary,
7. team up to establish a reading club for the class to collect and read varied readers. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: This is enhanced as the learner explores views to solve code word tables and

crossword puzzles using vocabulary.

• Learning to Learn: This is promoted as the learner builds on their own learning experience by finding meaning of new words

in simple level dictionaries.

22

Values:
• Unity: This is promoted as the learner works harmoniously to team up to establish a reading club for the class to collect

and read varied readers.

• Peace: This is enhanced as the learner displays tolerance when working with peers to conduct a reader’s theatre to read

stories.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is enhanced as the learner appreciates harmonious living with others in the society by obeying rules and

regulations, similar to obeying school rules.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of living together to similar content in Religious Education.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension,
2. infer the meaning of vocabulary from context for comprehension,
3. enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure.

Remember the key question: Why do we read silently? 2. What makes a book interesting to read?
